subject: SummitAI dedicated reserve — hardware tiering & memory/perf tradeoffs
messages:
From: Tariq Khan <tariq.khan@summitai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — Dedicated reserve SKU guidance for SummitAI

Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. SummitAI is finalizing a reserved capacity budget and procurement needs a short, decision-grade recommendation for GPU SKUs (H100 vs A100 vs L4) tied to our use case. I'm attaching a CSV with sample traffic shape and request types (gen vs embed). High level:

- Expected steady QPS: 400–700 depending on campaign spikes
- Peak concurrency windows: 10–15% of traffic in bursts
- Mixed workloads: ~35% embeddings (short context), ~65% text generation with mixed context lengths (avg 1k tokens, heavy tail up to 16k for fine-grained summaries)
- Latency SLO: p95 gen <= 200ms for online tier; embeddings p95 <= 50ms

Can you: 1) recommend an initial reserved pool breakdown (counts by SKU) with a short rationale focused on memory vs perf tradeoffs and 2) call out operational mitigations we should budget for (cache, burst, quantized variants)?

Attaching: summit_prod_workload.csv and the draft SOW (Summit_SOW_v1.pdf). Procurement is on copy (procurement@summitai.com).

Thanks — Tariq
Tariq Khan

Tariq — thanks for the data and SOW. Quick read and a few clarifying points before I put numbers behind it:

1) Can you confirm the percent of requests that are long-context (>= 8k tokens) vs short (<= 2k)? The CSV shows a heavy tail but we need the distribution to size KV cache memory.
2) Any hard SLA windows where burst > 1.5x steady is expected for > 30 minutes? That changes headroom planning.
3) Do you plan to use model variants (smaller embedding-only model + large gen model) or the same model family for both?

High level guidance up front so procurement has context:
- H100: best for long-context generative workloads — highest memory and single-GPU throughput for long KV caches and 16k+ seq lengths. Recommended where p95 latency and context state must be preserved without aggressive tiling.
- A100: balanced choice for mixed gen/throughput; good when you need dense throughput at moderate context sizes and can shard across 40/80GB variants. More cost-efficient than H100 for many gen workloads if you can accept some model quantization or sharding.
- L4: cost-optimized for high-volume embedding and short-context inference; lower memory and lower single-stream gen perf, but excellent price/perf for embedding pipelines and offline batch tasks.

I'll run a draft sizing and send a recommended reserve mix once you confirm the distribution.

— Kim

Kim — answers below + small edit to SOW attached:

- Long-context (>=8k tokens): ~18% of gen traffic, concentrated in nightly report generation and some analytics flows.
- Short-context (<=2k tokens): ~82%, mostly conversational assistants and webhooks.
- Burst windows: marketing campaigns can push 2x baseline for up to 45 minutes (historical). Plan for short pockets of sustained 1.8x for 1 hour in worst-case.
- Models: We expect to run two families: a distilled gen model (lower mem) for 90% of prod gen and a full-fidelity long-context model for the 10% heavy flows. Embeddings use a smaller embedding model (prod_embed_v2).

Also attaching Summit_SOW_v1.pdf (minor procurement comments). Can you include an ops-ready recommendation we can drop into the SOW? Procurement wants to sign but needs the SKU justification text.

Thanks — Tariq
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SummitAI workload answers — quick sizing guidance (need ops + cost inputs)

Team — forwarding SummitAI answers. Procurement wants SKU justification copy for the SOW and a recommended reserve pool. Draft sizing attached (summit_sizing_calc.xlsx). Key asks below and my draft recommendation. Please review and respond with ops caveats by EOD:

Requirements recap:
- Steady QPS: 400–700, bursts up to 2x (short windows).
- Workload split: 65% gen (18% long-context), 35% embeddings.
- Models: two gen families (distilled and full long-context).

Draft reserved pool recommendation (initial commit):
- 6 x H100 (reserved): purpose: long-context gen and canary of full-fidelity model. Rationale: H100 handles large KV cache + 16k seq without aggressive tiling; minimizes cross-GPU sharding for tail flows.
- 10 x A100 (reserved mix of 40GB/80GB): purpose: high-throughput gen for distilled model and medium-context requests. Rationale: better cost/perf at scale for majority gen traffic, flexible memory configs for sharding.
- 16 x L4 (reserved): purpose: embeddings and low-latency short-context inference (batching enabled). Rationale: best price/perf for embedding-heavy traffic and offline batch jobs.

Operational mitigations and notes:
- Cache sizing: reserve KV cache on H100s for long-context sessions; assume 20–30% memory overhead for KV state at 16k peaks.
- Batching & autoscale: configure continuous batching and per-route concurrency caps to keep p95 within SLOs. L4 pools should have larger batch windows for embeddings to drive cost efficiency.
- Fallbacks: shard to A100 pool or burst to host pool for overflow; use quantized variants for non-critical gen to reduce slot pressure.
- Headroom: plan for 20% spare capacity across the pool initially; this covers 1.8–2.0x short bursts without immediate scale-up.

Cost & procurement copy (short para for SOW):
"Redwood recommends a tiered reserved pool that balances memory-intensive tail flows and cost-efficient throughput. H100 nodes are reserved for the long-context model family to avoid cross-shard latency impacts; A100 nodes will serve the distilled/high-throughput gen workload; L4 nodes will be dedicated to embeddings and batch pipelines. The initial reserve mix provides operational headroom for short bursts and enables predictable unit economics while allowing automatic burst to additional capacity when needed."

Please validate the numbers (Dev) and add any quantization/tiling caveats (Aditya).

— Kim
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: SummitAI workload answers — quick sizing guidance (need ops + cost inputs)

Quick technical notes / caveats for the SOW copy:

- KV cache sizing: assume ~0.35–0.45 bytes per token in live KV state for the full-fidelity model due to attention caches + metadata. For a conservative 16k peak window expect ~6–8GB per active session of KV resident footprint. This is why H100 (higher HBM) is preferred for tail flows.
- A100 selection: prioritize a mix of 80GB A100s for model sharding (when serving 8k-ish contexts with replication) and 40GB A100s where throughput is king. The mix above can be tuned post-pilot based on per-route token distribution.
- L4 guidance: L4 is excellent for embeddings and short infer; recommend enabling int8/4 quant paths for L4 to maximize slot density. Avoid using L4 for any long-context gen unless strongly quantized and tested; the latency will climb and you risk increased tail latency.
- Autoscale and burst: include planned burst-to-host policy so that Reserved capacity stays within commit while occasional overflow uses on-demand capacity. Add a 30-minute cooldown to avoid flip-flopping.

Operational ask for SOW: line item for a pilot (2 weeks) to validate real traffic, plus a one-time services line for runtime tuning (cache config and route-level batching).

I'll append a short ops appendix (numbers and slot math) to the sizing workbook.

— Dev

Tariq — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the SOW comments. Based on Dev's caveats we've tightened the SOW paragraph and included a recommended pilot and ops appendix. High level next steps:

1) We drop the draft paragraph into the SOW (see attached link).
2) Pilot (2 weeks) to validate traffic and tune KV cache + batching. We recommend starting pilot with: 2 H100, 4 A100, 6 L4 for real traffic validation.
3) Post-pilot ramp to the reserved pool (6 H100 / 10 A100 / 16 L4) with a 20% headroom buffer and burst-to-host policy.

Estimated lead time: 6–8 weeks from PO to reserved capacity being fully provisioned (procurement timelines vary; specific lead times will be in the SOW appendix).

Estimated monthly reserved hardware cost (very rough ballpark for procurement): $220k–$290k/month depending on A100 40/80 mix and support tier. We'll provide a detailed quote once you confirm the A100 split.
